documents.text: Encryption protects data in transit. This encryption overview covers encryption keys, encryption modes, and the encryption standard roadmap for network traffic.
Backups run nightly. Backups are stored in two regions, backups are tested monthly, and backups at rest are covered by the platform default settings for backups.
A restore returns data from a backup. Restore requests, restore times, and restore drills are logged. Restore drills are part of the restore program.
The standard for encryption in transit is TLS 1.3. This standard names the standard ciphers, the standard handshake, and the standard certificates for services.
Fire drills run every spring. Safety drills, evacuation drills, and drills for severe weather follow the facilities calendar.
Nightly backups are sealed with AES-256 before transfer to offline storage. The sealing step is what protects the stored copies.
Restore rehearsals, called drills inside the operations team, happen every quarter. Each rehearsal rebuilds one service from the offline copies.
Storage tiers separate hot data from cold data. Tier changes are reviewed each quarter by the platform team.
Keys rotate every ninety days. Rotation is automatic, and failed rotations page the security team.
A full restore takes about four hours. Partial restores are faster, and restore progress is shown in the console.
The audit log records every administrative action. Logs are kept for one year and reviewed monthly.
Offline media is stored in a locked room. Access to the room requires two badges and a signed entry in the log.
